Title: A Novel Voice-Processing Method Leveraging Polyphonic Audio for Instrument Recognition Using Machine Learning
Source title: 2025 9th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation, ICCCBEA 2025
Abstract: In this research, a novel polyphonic voice recognition system for instrument identification, pitch detection, and chord detection based on machine learning techniques is presented. The system utilizes python and its large set of data analytics libraries to provide efficient and realistic audio recognition. Some of the main techniques involve Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction and classification models like k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) and hidden Markov models (hmm). MFCC s have been used to efficiently extract the spectral features of the audio signals, whereas K-NN classifiers (k=3) and hmm models (8 gaussian states) yield high instrument identification and sequential pattern audio analysis. The system also presents high accuracies of 58% using K-NN and 67% using hmm in classifying 8 instruments namely acoustic guitar, bass drum, cello, clarinet, double bass, flute, hi hat, saxophone, snare drum, violin. A stratified shuffle split strategy and a balanced dataset guarantee fair training and testing. The frontend, coded in html, CSS, and JavaScript, supports dynamic audio visualization and easy user interaction through web audio Api, whereas the backend, implemented with python and flask, processes real-time audio and machine learning operations. Iterative feedback-based updates enhance system flexibility even further, which makes it worthwhile for use in music education, production, transcription, and research applications. In spite of difficulties in overlapping sound separation and intricate polyphonic audio analysis, this research emphasizes the revolutionary potential of intelligent audio processing in developing music technology. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Hummer - Hum to search an audio query based music retrieval system
Source title: Recent Trends in Intelligent Computing and Communication: Volume 1
Abstract: Searching for music by humming a tune is a user-friendly approach that has long been a subject of interest in the field of music information retrieval. This study proposes a novel approach to audio-based query music search using humming inputs. The developed system employs a pre-trained Basic Pitch model to convert audio files into MIDI representations, which are then preprocessed and embedded in a low-dimensional form for semantic retrieval. By comparing these embeddings to humming inputs, the system identifies matching songs with high accuracy. A web application was made to test the proposed approach using React for the frontend and Flask and AstraDB for the backend. Title: Effects of Short Video Micro-Lessons on Solfeggio Performance Among Preschool Education Majors: A Cognitive Load Theory Quasi-Experiment
Source title: International Journal of Web-Based Learning and Teaching Technologies
Abstract: This study designed a mobile web-based adaptive microlearning system for solfeggio education, grounded in cognitive load theory. A dual closed-loop framework integrating real-time pitch detection via web audio application-programming interface, behavioral logging, and dynamic difficulty adjustment was designed to reduce extraneous load and activate germane load. A 4-week quasi-experiment with 120 preservice music teachers demonstrated significant performance gains in the microlearning group compared to face-to-face instruction, with baseline gaps narrowing from 24 to 9 points. Mediation analysis confirmed that performance improvement was driven by the path of extraneous load reduction → germane load increase, accounting for 35% of the total effect. The system offers a replicable paradigm for skill-based mobile learning. Title: Development of a Hummed-Based Query System for Music Retrieval
Source title: IEEE International Conference on Emerging and Sustainable Technologies for Power and ICT in a Developing Society, NIGERCON
Abstract: This research aims to improve query by humming (QBH) systems, enabling users to find music by humming a tune into a device. The project uses optimized database indexing, advanced machine learning techniques, and signal processing to process diverse humming inputs. Title: Analysis and Design of a Web-Based Vocal Music Auxiliary Teaching Platform
Source title: AIDME 2026 - Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Digital Media and Education
Abstract: Traditional vocal music instruction faces challenges such as difficulty in matching teachers and students across time and space, lack of personalized feedback, and absence of immediate guidance during practice. This study constructs a vocal music auxiliary teaching platform based on Web technologies, adopting a browser-server architecture. The frontend, built with the Vue.js framework, implements real-time pitch visualization and an interactive interface; the backend, based on the Flask framework, provides RESTful API services and integrates a pitch detection algorithm and a deep learning evaluation model. The system captures microphone input through the Web Audio API, extracts fundamental frequency using the YIN algorithm, and combines it with a deep neural network for pitch assessment and real-time feedback. Performance tests show that under a 100-user concurrent scenario, the platform achieves an average response time of 245.6 ms. User tests (N=20) yield a system usability score of 78.4, with average pitch deviation decreasing by 23.6% after practice. The study demonstrates that Web technologies can effectively support the real-time and interactive requirements of vocal music auxiliary teaching systems, although the assessment of complex timbre recognition and emotional expression dimensions still requires further optimization. Moreover, the current system does not yet support the evaluation of other critical vocal dimensions such as vibrato control, breath support, dynamics, or emotional expression, which are essential for holistic vocal development.  © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).
